whatItDoes: blob-basis.mjs (Node built-ins, read-only git) hashes a file on six bases (working copy and committed blob, each as-is, CRLF-folded and CRLF-synthesised; sha256, md5 and git blob id), gives a working-copy verdict (IDENTICAL / CRLF-CHECKOUT / EOL-ONLY / DIRTY, or UNTRACKED / NOT-ON-DISK / UNAVAILABLE with the reason), and places recorded hashes from --expect or a --scan of a provenance JSON as BLOB-, CRLF-, LF- or WORKTREE-BASIS, HISTORY or NO-MATCH, with --history, --against, --require and exit codes 0/1/2/3. At Aster 62ddb17 it places the cache's horizons and catalog hashes on the blob basis, earth-vz-span-max.json's c91f4e50... as the CRLF form (7,214,102 + 295,920 = 7,510,022 bytes), and the generator-script hash as NO-MATCH; on Skyhook it places the rev_a_md5 that 34935cb replaced on the CRLF basis. index.html shows those saved runs and runs the same basis.js on a file the reader picks, with the committed blob id pasted in because a browser has no git.
testsPin: The node tests (20; 19 run here, 1 skips because the clone is shallow) pin these external values. (1) Published vectors: FIPS 180 sha256 and SHA-1 "abc", the 448-bit message, the empty string; RFC 1321 md5. Each vector is also checked against node:crypto in the same test. (2) node:crypto on 600+ inputs, including every padding boundary and 1 MB. (3) git: `git hash-object --no-filters` and git's empty-blob id for blob ids, and `git hash-object --path=<text=auto path> --stdin` for CRLF folding. (4) The snapshots, recomputed with node:crypto and `git cat-file` at Aster 62ddb17 without basis.js: sha256(horizons blob) = the cache's horizonsFixtureSha256; blob bytes + LF count = earth-vz's recorded 7,510,022; sha256 of the split/join CRLF form = earth-vz's c91f4e50...; the catalog hash matches; the script hash matches neither form. (5) Skyhook 34935cb: md5 of params/rev_a.json's blob = rev_a_md5, and md5 of its CRLF form = the parent 27229e2's rev_a_md5. (6) The CLI must place exactly BLOB, BLOB, NO-MATCH, CRLF, with --require blob exiting 1. (7) Real CRLF, mixed and edited copies of an Aster fixture give CRLF-CHECKOUT, EOL-ONLY and DIRTY, and git's own filter agrees only on the first two. (8) --history names the commit git rev-list gives for an older STATUS.md. (9) The README quotes the recomputed hashes and byte counts, and example.txt/example-data.js match a fresh run. ui-check.mjs (80 checks, at 390 px dark and 1280 px light) asserts the page's numbers against example-data.js and a sum it recomputes, plus verdicts, refusals and a real file through the input. Sabotage, each run on a copy (node failures / ui failures): toCrlf CR after LF 11/5; toLf drops LF 7/11; blob header space instead of NUL 2/0; CLI blob id off by one 2/0; CRLF-CHECKOUT loosened 2/2; CRLF-BASIS before BLOB-BASIS 1/0; SHA-256 K from sqrt 3/0; MD5 shift 8 3/0; scan ignores sibling path 3/0; CLI exit 0 on NO-MATCH 1/0; history skips oldest commit 1/0; inferBlob as-is only 1/9; CRLF stats bytes 1/0; prefix anywhere 1/0; 7-hex prefix 1/0; page arithmetic 0/4; page family order 0/2; page ignores blob id 0/15. Every sabotage is caught by at least one suite; six are caught by a single test and nothing else.

deviationsFromProposal:
- Six bases instead of four. The CRLF form of the blob is what a CRLF checkout writes, and CRLF(disk) only equals it when the working copy is clean.
- CRLF-CHECKOUT now requires disk == CRLF(blob) exactly. EOL-ONLY is new, for a copy with the same content but mixed or other line endings. The proposal's "mixed-EOL fixture is DIRTY" now applies only when the content also differs.
- The proposal's premise of a CRLF checkout (STATUS.md:458) is stale at 62ddb17: the checkout is LF (S19-D04), so every working-copy verdict is IDENTICAL. The tool's value is reconciling existing records and gating new ones, and the tagline states the findings instead of "so OQ-17-7 stops recurring".
- The scan finds four recorded hashes, not two: 2 BLOB-BASIS, 1 CRLF-BASIS, and 1 NO-MATCH for the generator script. Tracing the NO-MATCH produced Finding 1.
- Added beyond the proposal: md5 and git-blob-id matching and hex prefixes; --history, --against, --require and --brief; exit codes 0/1/2/3 following PartForge's headless convention; Skyhook reconciliations (current and parent decision_grid); the MCP baked-asset run; and index.html with an in-browser checker that infers the blob from a pasted blob id. The proposal's surface was CLI only.
- The landing now starts at Slice 19.5 Front D3 (SLICE_19_5_FOUNDING.md:305-306), the open scheduled item, instead of only SLICE_17_FOUNDING.md.
- The earth-vz snapshot picks generatedAtUtc, source and fixture rather than fixture alone. Two Skyhook snapshots were added, one of them derived from history by build-data.mjs.
- The Skyhook snapshot is named decision_grid.keys.json because the checker treats any *.provenance.json file as a sidecar.
